RSR.help.plots.title: Plots, State and Phases
RSR.help.plots.body.gm: A Plot is one running situation — an invasion, an investigation, a fragile treaty. It carries a single number, its State, and the bands along that number are its Phases. You name each Phase and set the threshold it starts at. The table only ever sees the label of the Phase the Plot is in right now, never the ones waiting further up the track, so you can write "Rain of Fire" today without warning anyone it exists.
RSR.help.plots.body.player: A Plot is one running situation your characters care about — an invasion, an investigation, a treaty that may not hold. The bar is how far it has swung, and the word beside it names where things stand at the moment. It is not a countdown to anything you have been told about; it describes now.
RSR.help.threads.title: Threads
RSR.help.threads.body.gm: Threads are the moving parts of a Plot. Each fills toward its own threshold, and when one concludes it moves the Plot's State by whatever you set for the Force that concluded it. Threads belong to the Plot rather than to any Force, so more than one side can push the same Thread in opposite directions. A Thread can be locked behind others, and a locked Thread never names a prerequisite the viewer cannot already see.
RSR.help.threads.body.player: Threads are the moving parts of a Plot — the things being attempted inside it. Each has its own bar. When one finishes it shifts the whole Plot, for better or worse depending on who got there. Some Threads are waiting on others, and some you are only told exist.
RSR.help.state.title: What you are allowed to see
RSR.help.state.body.gm: Every Plot, Thread, Force and Asset is Visible, Masked or Hidden, with a separate switch for whether its numbers show. Masked means the row still appears but reads as ??? — the table knows something is there. Hidden means it is never drawn for them: the board does not put it on their screen at all. Use Visible with values hidden when the table should know a Thread is running without knowing how close it is. One caveat worth knowing: this hides things from play, not from a determined cheat. Foundry copies world data to every connected client, so a player who goes looking in the developer console can read what is stored. Treat it as a screen, not a vault.
RSR.help.state.body.player: Some of this board is deliberately incomplete. A row reading ??? is something you know exists but not what it is. A bar with no numbers is something you can see moving without knowing how far it has to go. And there will be Threads you are not shown at all — that is the GM keeping the world larger than your current information, which is the whole point of the thing.
RSR.help.tryBody: Builds a complete Plot — two rival Forces, all four Thread modes, a prerequisite chain, and a spread of visibility states. It is real data, so you can edit it, break it and watch the board react. Everything it makes is tagged, and Remove deletes exactly that and nothing you wrote yourself.
RSR.help.removeExampleWarning: Remove every entry the example created? Anything you authored yourself is untouched.
RSR.help.examplePresent: The example is currently in this world.
RSR.settings.defaultVisibility.name: Default visibility for new entries
RSR.settings.defaultVisibility.hint: What players can see about a Plot, Thread, Force or Asset the moment it is created, before you have set its visibility by hand. Hidden is the safe default: nothing you jot down mid-session leaks to the table until you choose to reveal it.
RSR.settings.boardMenu.hint: Opens the Situation Room. The usual way in is the button at the top of the Journal sidebar; this is here in case that sidebar has been customised out from under it.
